scope.root_cause: ProcessManager.accept_review re-verified only the worker's own changed/output-path hashes before promote(); a declared dependency/input artifact (e.g. B912's canonical output) could advance between claim time and promotion with no check at all, so a retained-worktree validation that passed against a stale input snapshot (29 rows) was silently promoted after the canonical dependency had already advanced (3,522 rows).
changes: process_launcher._path_manifest(base, declared): bounded, deterministic manifest for declared repo-relative paths -- a file entry records sha256/size/line_count, a directory entry records only entry_count plus a listing_sha256 over immediate children's name+size (never recursive content hashing), so cost is proportional to the declared path count, never a broad repository walk
ProcessManager._launch_isolated captures the immutable_inputs manifest from the canonical repo immediately before task_engine.claim_start_exact (input A) and threads it through metadata.json
ProcessManager._finalize_isolated_request copies the declared immutable_inputs + claim-time manifest into the review_ready terminal_review evidence unchanged

ProcessManager.accept_review recomputes the current canonical manifest for the same declared paths immediately before promote() and fails closed with stale_input:dependency_changed:<path> on any mismatch -- no promote() call, no task_engine.accept_review call, canonical repo and task status left exactly as in review
guard is a no-op when a card declares no immutable_inputs at all -- existing scope/required-output/validation/idempotence gates are unaffected

acceptance_evidence.requirement: claim at input A, canonical input mutation to B, then accept_review fails with stale_input/dependency_changed before promotion
canonical output paths and task finished-state remain unchanged on mismatch
unchanged immutable input/dependency hashes still accept and promote exactly once, including on an idempotent retry
tasks declaring no immutable_inputs are unaffected by the new guard
directory manifests never content-hash children and detect population growth via entry_count
a missing declared path manifests as a bounded {kind: missing}, never an exception

forbidden_regressions.promotion_before_input_revalidation: the new guard runs before promote()/task_engine.accept_review() and returns before either is ever called on mismatch
forbidden_regressions.hash_bypass: declared immutable_inputs are re-read from the canonical repo at accept_review time, never trusted from stale evidence alone
forbidden_regressions.broad_repository_snapshot: _path_manifest only ever touches the declared paths themselves; a directory entry lists immediate children only and never recurses
forbidden_regressions.host_global_state: the manifest comparison reads only self.repo (the bound per-ProcessManager repository), never ambient/global state

environment_note: This worktree is a sparse checkout of only the four allowed_writes files under src/aiworkhub (core.py, process_launcher.py, task_engine.py, task_store.py); every other sibling module (repository_state, callback_store, task_plan, dependency_autolaunch, storage_registry, runtime_adapters, worker_ai_tools_mcp, worker_workspace, provider_tool_guards, task_fsm) is absent, and pytest itself is not installed and could not be installed (sandboxed pip/venv writes are rejected). The test file installs lenient stand-in modules for the absent siblings (mirroring the existing _ensure_deepseek_credentials_stub/_ensure_aiworkhub_sibling_stubs precedent) so the real, unmodified core.py/task_engine.py/process_launcher.py import and run unchanged. All 7 tests were verified to pass by executing them directly against the real production code with a hand-built monkeypatch/tmp_path harness (pytest's own collector was unavailable in this sandbox); the listed pytest command is expected to pass unchanged wherever pytest is installed.
